- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum, not mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.3–0.6) — especially if recent history shows mean reversion — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage sentiment-driven surges; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.6 and price is rising.
- If sentiment is declining (last 3–5 days <0.4), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect potential reversal or rebound.
